Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0059", "row_sha256": "29ae1979f5bde1f86da03d384093df77a261bb219d8e40a64f4855eb68d7fa91", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you make this into a usable prompt for planning next week's greenhouse watering rota, not the rota itself. it should ask for one Monday to Sunday plan and say clearly that the finished rota is for Tess, not Idris. i want the useful details below kept together, and no one should be given a shift at a time they aren't available. if something can't be covered from the people and times here, ask the planner to show the gap instead of guessing who can do it. the greenhouse is the old glasshouse behind the community plot, about twelve metres long. we divide it into west bench, centre bed, east bed, and propagation bench; those are the names people actually use, so keep them as written. there's a narrow path between the two beds and only one hose that reaches the far end, so don't plan simultaneous hose jobs. the watering can stays beside the propagation bench and is separate from the hose.

this is a rota for ordinary care, not a redesign of the beds. West bench has the tomatoes, in two rows labelled W1 and W2, and those need checking every day. check the soil before watering them; the usual morning check is enough, but if the top few centimetres still feel damp, don't water just because the rota says tomatoes. Centre bed is the herbs, labelled C1, and needs a daily morning check too. The east bed has four citrus tubs. They are normally watered Tuesday and Friday only when the top three centimetres are dry, not automatically on both days. On the propagation bench, the seed trays need a light mist in the morning and another look in the afternoon every day. don't turn that afternoon look into an instruction to water if they don't need it. There are two orchids on the shelf above the sink; follow the date written on each pot label, and don't add a routine watering day for them. one label currently says 14 May and the other says 18 May, but the rota covers the week starting 12 May, so keep those label dates visible rather than deciding either date is wrong.

The available watering windows are 7 to 9 in the morning and 5 to 6 in the evening. There is a key in the plot office, and nobody should be assigned a morning job before 7 or an evening job after 6. Tess can do Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings, or Sunday evening. Idris is available Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and not Saturday. Jo can do Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Len can do Wednesday and Friday evenings and Saturday morning. No availability was given for Sunday morning, or for anyone at another time, so don't fill those in. Tess may also take a shift when she's available; the important thing is who receives the finished rota. don't send it to Idris instead.

please make the prompt ask for a rota that spreads jobs across the available people and makes clear which work is a check, which is conditional watering, and which is a scheduled light mist. For tomatoes and citrus, the person on duty should make the soil check first and water only if the stated condition is met. The daily centre-bed check should be shown as a check, not silently turned into extra watering. Keep propagation's morning mist and afternoon look distinct. A person can cover more than one area in a window, but the single hose means no two hose-based jobs can be listed as happening at the same time. The watering can at propagation can be used separately. don't assume travel time or make up a different way to water anything.

Mara, who checks the greenhouse most weeks, said, “The west bench dries first after noon.” Include that as a note for the planner, but don't let it override the stated check-before-watering rule or turn it into a fixed extra watering. There is no measured moisture log supplied, so the prompt should not ask the rota to claim which beds will actually be dry on a particular day. If the person planning needs to show a conditional job, make the condition visible beside it. Use the week starting 12 May, and keep the dates on the orchid labels in the information rather than assigning them a routine.

I need a compact plan that's readable when printed and can be copied onto the whiteboard by the greenhouse door. ask for a short opening note explaining the check-first and conditional items, then one numbered section for the Monday-to-Sunday rota, with day, time window, person, area, and action all easy to find. after that, ask for a brief note of any uncovered availability or task gap. don't have the prompt ask for a weekly total or a claim that everything is covered, since nothing says that it will be. The whiteboard is wiped each Monday morning, and the person copying the rota will use the key from the plot office; those are practical details, not extra shifts. keep this within the greenhouse and the coming week. there is no request to change labels, buy supplies, or decide what the plants need beyond the checks and conditions listed here.", "output": "Create one Monday-to-Sunday watering rota for the week starting 12 May for the old glasshouse behind the community plot. Address the finished rota to **Tess, not Idris**. Keep the plan within the greenhouse and the coming week; do not make the rota itself a redesign of the beds. Use the area names as written: west bench, centre bed, east bed, and propagation bench. The greenhouse is about twelve metres long. A narrow path runs between the two beds, and there is one hose that reaches the far end, so do not schedule two hose-based jobs at the same time. The watering can beside the propagation bench is separate from the hose.

Use only the stated availability. The permitted windows are 7 to 9 in the morning and 5 to 6 in the evening; do not assign anyone before 7 in the morning or after 6 in the evening. Tess is available Monday, Wednesday, and Friday mornings, and Sunday evening. Idris is available Tuesday and Thursday mornings, but not Saturday. Jo is available Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday evenings. Len is available Wednesday and Friday evenings, and Saturday morning. Tess may be assigned a shift when she is available, but she is the recipient of the finished rota. No availability is given for Sunday morning or for anyone at any other time, so do not fill in those gaps by assumption. Spread jobs across available people where possible. If the listed people and times do not cover a task, show the gap rather than guessing who could take it. A person may cover more than one area in a window, subject to the single-hose limitation.

The plant-care instructions are as follows. The west bench contains tomatoes in two rows labelled W1 and W2; check them every day and check the soil before watering. The usual morning check is enough. If the top few centimetres are still damp, do not water them just because the rota lists the tomatoes. The centre bed contains herbs labelled C1 and needs a daily morning check; show that as a check, not as extra watering. The east bed has four citrus tubs, normally considered on Tuesday and Friday only. Water them on those days only if the top three centimetres are dry. On the propagation bench, give the seed trays a light mist in the morning and another look in the afternoon every day. Keep the afternoon look distinct from the morning mist, and do not turn the afternoon check into an instruction to water when it is not needed. The two orchids on the shelf above the sink should be handled according to the dates written on their pot labels, not given a routine watering day. One label says 14 May and the other says 18 May. Keep both dates visible; the rota covers the week starting 12 May, and the dates are not supplied as an error to correct.

Make clear which rota items are checks, which involve conditional watering, and which are scheduled light misting. For tomatoes and citrus, show the soil check before any watering and make the condition visible beside the task. Do not treat the west bench as needing extra water on a fixed schedule. Mara, who checks the greenhouse most weeks, said, “The west bench dries first after noon.” Include this as a note for the planner, without letting it override the check-before-watering rule or convert it into a fixed additional watering job. No measured moisture log is supplied, so do not claim which areas will actually be dry on a particular day. Do not assume travel time or invent another watering method.

Format the result for printing and copying onto the whiteboard by the greenhouse door, which is wiped each Monday morning. Begin with a short note explaining check-first and conditional tasks. Then include one numbered section containing the Monday-to-Sunday rota, with the day, time window, person, area, and action easy to find. Finish with a brief note of any uncovered availability or task gap. Do not ask the rota to include a weekly total or claim that everything is covered. The person copying it will use the key in the plot office; treat that as a practical detail, not an extra shift. Do not add requests to change labels, buy supplies, or decide what the plants need beyond the checks and conditions listed here."}]
